text:
Maya Patel: Quick RFC follow-up — I'm proposing an "epochal" refactor approach I've been calling 'stagger & ride' for the orchestration plane. TL;DR: incremental decomposition by traffic-shard + live traffic steering (mirror, shadow, weighted rollouts) and a compatibility shim so the monolith stays live as we migrate tenants. Want feedback on safety nets and migration pacing. :eyes:

Chris Nguyen: sounds promising. main questions: how do we handle KV cache ownership transitions? and what's the cutover signal? p99 latency spikes?

Maya Patel: Good Q. For KV we keep read-through proxy for a wave (reads from new store, fall back to old), writes go to both with idempotency token. Cutover signal = sustained <5% error delta + stable p99 for 30m, otherwise auto rollback.

Devon R.: Concern: double-writes mean increased write QPS. Need to cap fanout and add a backpressure path. Suggest an intermediary write-queue with at-most-once retries and TTL. Also need a schema compatibility plan for the cache keys.

Sasha Liao: Ops constraints: any rollout that increases tail latency by >10% triggers immediate roll back. We should preflight with a 1% mirroring window and run a synthetic workload that mirrors 100% of real request shapes. Also add a runbook snippet for circuit-breaker trips.

Aria (eng-sre): I'll own the alerts and experiment dashboards. Metrics we need in the canary: p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, cache hit ratio, inter-service queue depth, 5m request success rate. Also add a 'staleness' gauge for the read-proxy fallback rate.

Maya Patel: Nice list. For monitoring I want these thresholds: p99 < baseline + 8ms, error rate delta < 0.5%, fallback-rate < 0.2% after 10m. If threshold breached, route weight drops 50% and we spin new canary.

Chris Nguyen: How about ownership of the orchestration API surface? We need a compatibility shim that accepts both old and new shapes and emits warnings to logs. Plan: 6-week spike to implement shim + telemetry, then 8-week rollout (10/25/50/75/100) per tenant cohort.

Maya Patel: Agreed. Sketch of rollout command we'll use: ```
redwood rollout start --target orchestration-v2 \
  --strategy weighted --waves 5 \
  --metrics p99,error_rate,cache_fallback \
  --auto-rollback on-threshold
```

Devon R.: Add a migration flag header so clients can opt-in per-tenant for the first two waves: `X-ORCH-MIGRATE: wave-1`. That helps debugging.

Sasha Liao: We'll need a short-lived feature flag gate per tenant in the control plane. Ops will toggle if we see noise. Keep the gate metadata in tenant config and emit structured events.

deploy-bot: RFC doc uploaded: <https://redwood.internal/rfcs/epochal-refactor-stagger-and-ride> (v1). Deployment scaffolding PRs: #4123 #4130. :robot_face:

Maya Patel: Next steps: I'll update the RFC with KV double-write sketch and explicit rollback flows. Devon — can you prototype the write-queue shim during the spike? Aria — set up dashboards and a synthetic traffic profile. Sasha — write the runbook entries. Target: spike complete in 2 weeks, then we reconvene. :thumbsup:

Chris Nguyen: +1. One more ask: let's add a small, automated smoke test that runs after each weight change — 10 warmup requests + 100 test requests matching p95 sequence lengths. If smoke fails, auto-decrease weight.

Maya Patel: Good call. I'll add that to the rollout script. Thanks everyone — posting this summary in the RFC thread too. :pray:
